content:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: hardware instability detected on node infer-3. Multiple driver resets reported over the last 6m, elevated ECC correctable count, and container restarts. PD:PD-INC-2105000000. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-driver-resets

Alice (SRE): I’m on it. Notified on-call HW. Mateo, can you pull the live metrics? I want GPU reset count, ECC c-rate, and pod restart rates for the last 15m.

Mateo (Infra): grabbing dashboards now. Quick summary: GPU driver resets spiked from 0 -> 5 across infer-3 in the last 4m. ECC correctable errors went from ~10/hr -> ~120 in the same window. Pod restarts correlate: 3 model-serving pods OOM/restart. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/gpu-infra/infer-3?orgId=1

Priya (EngRuntime): seeing client errors surfaced as 502/503 in the logs for the affected pods. Also some inference jobs timed out with CUDA Xid 13 and Xid 79. Sample from container logs:

```
[2026-03-15T21:33:42Z] inference-server ERROR: CUDA error at /workspace/runtime/src/device.cu:234: Xid (13) -> GPU reset
[2026-03-15T21:33:42Z] inference-server WARN: KV cache lost for session=abc123
[2026-03-15T21:34:01Z] runtime OOM: killed process 2345 (inference) total-vm:12G, anon-rss:9.6G
```

Alice (SRE): run a quick `kubectl describe pod` on one of the restarted pods and paste dmesg from the node. Also check `nvidia-smi -q` for ECC stats.

Mateo (Infra): output snippets below:

```
$ kubectl describe pod inference-xyz -n prod
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  10m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned prod/inference-xyz to infer-3
  Warning BackOff    6m    kubelet            Back-off restarting failed container
```

From node infer-3 (`dmesg | tail -n 40`):
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (13): .. GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457001] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x23)
[  123.458234] mlx5 0000:81:00.0: GPU ECC corrected errors increased
[  125.900001] oom-kill: constraint breach, killed process 2345 (inference)
```

`nvidia-smi -q` ECC section shows Correctable Errors: 0 -> 87 in last 10m for GPU0.

Priya (EngRuntime): Container OOMs look like secondary effect — driver resets cause memory fragmentation then kernel OOM. We should evac inference workloads off infer-3 ASAP then reboot the node and re-run driver diagnostics.

Alice (SRE): Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan:
- cordon infer-3 (`kubectl cordon infer-3`)
- drain non-critical pods with `kubectl drain infer-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` (keep a couple of canary replicas on other nodes)
- restart nvidia driver: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` post-evac
- hardware team to run ECC scrub and hardware diagnostics

Mateo (Infra): cordoning now. K8s drain in progress. Notifying autoscaler to avoid scheduling back.

infra-bot: cordon action taken by Mateo (Infra) at 2026-03-15T21:34:45Z. Node infer-3 is cordoned.

Hardware Team: we need immediate ECC scrub and memory test on infer-3. Possible DIMM degradation or GPU memory bitflips causing repeated Xid resets. Can you triage?

Hardware Team: acknowledged — starting ECC scrub and scheduling GPU firmware/driver diagnostics. If errors persist after scrub we'll plan a replacement GPU. ETA for initial results: 30-45m.

Priya (EngRuntime): short-term customer impact: requests routed to affected pods returned intermittent 5xx for ~4m while resets were occurring. We saw latency spikes: p50 from 150ms -> 850ms, p95 > 3s. No data exfiltration concerns.

Customer Success: flagged three customers with high request rates to this cluster. Reached out to their AEs and notified them of degraded latency and intermittent errors; they asked for ETA — will share once we have remediation steps.

Alice (SRE): action update — drain completed. All model-serving replicas rescheduled to healthy nodes except two stateful services we pinned; we manually scaled them down then up. Rebooting infer-3 now.

Mateo (Infra): reboot issued: `sudo reboot` at 21:36:10. Node status will show NotReady during reboot.

oncall-bot: Incident severity remains P1 due to customer impact. Please annotate when you complete driver restart and hardware scrub.

Priya (EngRuntime): after reboot, nvidia driver loaded but still seeing ECC correctable spikes (small). Running `nvidia-smi --query-ecc=corrected --format=csv` shows decreasing trend after scrub started. Collecting further logs.

Hardware Team: ECC scrub completed. Summary: DIMM and GPU memory tests show transient correctable ECC events localized to GPU0; no uncorrectable errors. Firmware applied to GPU microcode (v2.14), rebooted once more. Recommendation: monitor for 24h; if spikes return, swap out GPU card.

Alice (SRE): rolling the node back into service: `kubectl uncordon infer-3` at 21:58:30. Observability: post-fix driver resets stopped, pod restarts no longer correlated. Marking incident as mitigated but still monitoring.

Customer Success: communicated to customers: brief outage window with degraded latency, mitigation performed, will follow up with post-incident report.

Mateo (Infra): adding proactive alert: ECC-correctable-rate > 50/min for a node -> create low-severity ticket and schedule a scrub before it reaches P1.

Alice (SRE): Handoff to morning oncall (Priya) — please take 24h watch and ping if any new Xid/ECC spikes. I’ll draft a short postmortem with timeline and RCA notes.

Priya (EngRuntime): taking handoff. Will keep an eye and validate that client error rates return to baseline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. New on-call: Priya (EngRuntime). Previous on-call (Alice (SRE)) marked incident as mitigated at 2026-03-15T21:59:00Z.

Alice (SRE): next steps for the postmortem: collect kernel logs, driver logs, ECC counts, and container OOM traces; correlate with scheduled maintenance windows; propose playbook update to include automatic cordon+drain when Xid>3 in 5m.

Mateo (Infra): will open infra ticket INFRA-2105 to schedule GPU replacement if repeated correctables appear.

Hardware Team: will arrange replacement pool hardware and test bench evaluation in case of recurrence.

Customer Success: will send customer follow-up after postmortem.

Alice (SRE): closing thread for now — monitoring continues. If anyone sees a new spike, re-open or create follow-up incident thread.
